<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>ae683f770</title>

    *::after {
      box-sizing: border-box;
      margin: 0;
      padding: 0;
    }

    html,
    body {
      height: 100%;
    }

    body {
      min-height: 100vh;
      display: grid;
      place-items: center;
      padding: 1rem;
      background: #fafafa;
      color: #111;
    }

    svg {
      display: block;
      width: min(400px, 100%);
      height: auto;
      aspect-ratio: 1 / 1;
    }

    circle {
      fill: currentColor;
    }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <svg id="ae683f770" viewBox="0 0 400 400" role="img" aria-labelledby="ae683f770-title">
    <title id="ae683f770-title">Black circle</title>
    <circle cx="200" cy="200" r="200"/>
  </svg>
</body>
</html>

content.text:
Updated `0.html` with these changes:

- **Fixed overflow.** The body used `width: 100vw`, which causes a horizontal scrollbar when a vertical scrollbar is present. It now uses `min-height` and a grid for centering.
- **Responsive SVG.** The circle was fixed at 400px and would clip on narrow screens. It now scales down to fit the viewport while keeping a square aspect ratio.
- **Accessibility.** Added `role="img"`, a `<title>`, and `aria-labelledby` so screen readers describe the graphic.
- **Explicit styling.** Added `box-sizing: border-box`, a light background, and the circle fills from `currentColor` so it can be recolored via CSS.

The visual result is unchanged on desktop: a centered black circle.
